summary.headline: Cyient DLM Q4 FY26 revenue fell 13.8% YoY to INR3,691 million, while order book hit a record INR24,166 million and FY26 EBITDA margin stayed above 10%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR3,691 million, down 13.8% YoY, which management attributed to a large A&D order completion in Q4 FY25 and West Asia-related material delays and customer schedule slippage. Quarterly EBITDA was INR431 million (11.7% margin) and PAT was INR224 million (6.1%), both the highest margins of FY26 on a sequential basis. For FY26, revenue fell 17% to INR12,615 million, normalized EBITDA was INR1,302 million (10.3%), and reported PAT rose 7.7% to INR733 million. The order book closed at a record INR24,166 million, with FY26 order intake above $208 million and book-to-bill of 1.5x. Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance but expects YoY growth in every quarter of FY27.

financial_highlights.change: INR672 million net addition in Q4; INR5,105 million higher than last year

financial_highlights.metric: Rest of world share of revenue

segments.name: Defense
segments.commentary: Defense share of revenue is low, down 68% YoY as a large order ended in FY25.

segments.name: Aerospace, industrial and medical
segments.commentary: Management named these as the largest industry contributors by revenue; non-A&D is growing and is a stated focus.

segments.name: Build-to-spec (B2S)
segments.commentary: First year of B2S revenue; management called it a long-term play with series volume in a couple of years. The 'Others' category grew strongly on B2S and value-added offerings.

segments.name: Altek (US)
segments.commentary: US business carries a lower EBITDA margin; cross-sell synergies have only started on a trial basis, with the first Altek PO from a Cyient DLM standalone synergy customer in Q4.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 revenue guidance; management expects YoY growth in all four quarters of FY27, supported by the order book.
Management expects to sustain double-digit EBITDA margins, with a couple of basis points of improvement from operating leverage as volumes grow.
Working capital target of about 100 to 120 days; management said it would take a couple of years.
Mass-manufacturing orders from four new anchor clients are expected from Q3-Q4 FY27, with scaling in FY28.
Long-lead materials for the entire FY27 have been ordered for critical items, to support FY27 commitments.
Revenue shortfall from Q4 has partly moved into Q1 FY27 according to management.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed in the call.
Management said it is focused on vertical integration across cable, sheet metal and machining, as part of the 'expand' phase.
Management is investing in automation to support scalable growth.
demand_pricing: Order pipeline is close to $0.5 billion, per management; FY27 order intake targets are being driven internally.
Order book is defined as customer purchase orders; TCV is excluded (a five-year TCV of about $40 million was cited as excluded from intake).
Inventory days stayed elevated in FY26 due to long-lead component stocking; management reports a reduction in Q4. DSO improved from the low 90s to the mid-70s.
Customers were delayed by West Asia-related cargo disruptions via Dubai and Doha, plus defense approvals and NPA approvals from customers.
US tariff uncertainty persists; management expects clarity possibly within about one quarter.
Memory chip lead times have lengthened, which is affecting electronic component availability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue miss the YoY expectation given in the Q3 call?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited West Asia-related material delays from the Middle East, delayed approvals on Israeli defense programs, and customer NPA approvals; Q4 revenue was pushed into Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How does management define order book versus order intake?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book and intake count only customer purchase orders that are executable in the current or later years, excluding TCV; the book is 18 to 24 months in range.

qa_highlights.question: Can the amount of revenue deferred be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify the deferred revenue, saying only that three areas hit Q4 and that the order book supports QoQ growth.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company expect FY27 growth of 25% to 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a numerical guidance and said FY27 would be a strong year, with the Q4 QoQ growth and visibility supporting that view.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone EBITDA margin fall in Q4 and is it due to Altek investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the US business has a structurally lower margin, that tariffs are weighing on Altek, and that cross-pollination benefits have only begun on a trial basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a structural issue behind weak growth relative to peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the FY25 order intake shortfall to the need for organizational changes, and said the FY26 order intake growth of 35-40% is comparable to peers; sales hiring is ongoing.

risks_watch: Execution risk from West Asia logistics, cargo routing via Dubai and Doha, and Israeli defense program approvals.
Memory and electronic component shortages with longer lead times, which pressure inventory and gross margin.
Working capital elevated; inventory days still high despite Q4 reduction.
US tariff overhang on Altek and cross-sell synergies that have yet to scale.
Whether the new sales hires convert into order intake, as FY27 growth depends on it.
Other expenses rose from INR29 crore to INR44 crore YoY, as cited by an analyst; management attributed this to a mix of US and India operations and said it would be fixed in nature.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the order book and margins, but evasive on FY27 numbers: management declined to give revenue guidance or quantify deferred revenue, and attributed the FY26 shortfall to external factors and a weak FY25 order intake.
key_quotes: This is the first time that we've ended with a 10% plus EBITDA margin for the entire year, and we believe that we are in a very sustainable situation.
The order book reached its highest level in last 10 quarters.
So there is no structural challenges, anything in the organization because we are running the business for several years.

growth.why: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance; management expects YoY growth in all four quarters of FY27, backed by a record INR24,166m order book (book-to-bill 1.5x in FY26) and anchor-client mass-manufacturing orders from Q3-Q4 FY27, though no capacity additions were disclosed.
